findings.title: Negative slice start raises ValueError in Django QuerySet
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` (the comment claiming the ORM handles it is false). Any request with a negative cursor offset against this endpoint will produce an unhandled 500. The same applies in `BasePaginator.get_result` line 182 where negative offsets are still passed through when `cursor.is_prev` is true.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle datetime keys
findings.body: `get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to `getattr(item, self.key)`. The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime`, and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. Likewise `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value, which is then compared against a datetime column in `build_queryset`, producing invalid SQL/incorrect filtering. Requests with `optimized_pagination=true` will fail or return wrong pages; a DateTime-aware key implementation (like `DateTimePaginator`) is required.

findings.title: Offset clamping made inconsistent with later length check
findings.body: `BasePaginator.get_result` now slices from `start_offset = max(0, offset)` but the subsequent prev-page trimming still compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the unclamped `offset`. When `offset` differs from `start_offset` (negative offsets) the trim condition can never match, so the extra fetched row is returned to the client, producing an over-sized page and wrong next/prev cursors. The clamping logic should be applied consistently, or negative offsets rejected as before.

findings.title: Client-controlled query param selects paginator that bypasses offset bounds
findings.body: `optimized_pagination=true` is a user-supplied query parameter that switches to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`, which explicitly permits offsets outside normal pagination bounds (negative OFFSET/cursor values). The in-code justification that "permissions are checked at the queryset level" is only true for the organization filter; arbitrary offsets are not a permission boundary and expose unvalidated, error-prone query paths to any superuser or member with global access. Either remove the parameter or validate offsets server-side.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError
findings.body: `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated whenever `request.user.is_superuser` is false. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `None` for requests that are not made by an organization member (e.g. token/sentry-app auth or a staff user outside the org), so this will raise `AttributeError` and return a 500 on an endpoint that previously worked. Guard with `organization_context.member and ...`.

findings.title: Misleading comment about negative offsets in Cursor
findings.body: The added comment states that negative offsets are allowed as a "performance optimization" enabling reverse pagination, but `Cursor` performs no validation at all and downstream paginators cannot actually use negative offsets (Django queryset slicing rejects them). The comment misdocuments behaviour and encourages callers to construct invalid cursors.

findings.title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and the new `optimized_pagination` branch of the audit log endpoint are added without any unit or API tests. The datetime key bug and negative-offset ValueError would both have been caught by a basic test exercising the new branch.
